visual_text: Quinine for night cramps: time for a review?
Man: 'I've taken quinine for my cramps for ages. Is it still doing anything?'
Pharmacist: 'In trials, cramps fell from about 9 to 6 or 7 a fortnight, on low-quality evidence. Rare harms can be serious.'
Pharmacist: 'UK prescribing advice has been to pause it every 3 months to check. Could any of your other medicines be linked?'
Man: 'So we pause it, and I try calf stretches before bed.'
Under the last panel: no harms were reported in small stretching trials; evidence for benefit is mixed
El-Tawil et al., Cochrane 2015; Rabbitt et al., Age Ageing 2016; Coppin et al., Br J Gen Pract 2005; Garrison et al., Arch Intern Med 2012; Hawke et al., Cochrane 2021
alt_text: Illustrative four-panel comic, not real people. An older man asks a pharmacist whether quinine for night cramps still helps. She gives the trial figures, advises a pause every 3 months and a medicines check; he pauses it and tries calf stretches. Evidence for benefit is mixed.
